quotes.text: Do not waste your essence teaching stones to swim.
test carefully with strangers, abandon quickly those who exploit, but deepen generously with those who reciprocate.
She sent one stone forward, the smallest offering that still held meaning.
"Why share when you can possess? Your sister's generosity is weakness to exploit."
The First River, receiving emptiness, could return only emptiness.
once reciprocity is proven, the testing must evolve into building.
**The Myth of the Eighth River's Patience**
"Why waste even one stone on stillness?" asked a passing cloud.
Wisdom distinguishes between rivers that choose hoarding and those wounded into stillness.
Philosophy without sustained practice is just elaborate justification for remaining sealed.

note: Numbered rivers: test strangers, abandon exploiters, deepen with reciprocators; one-stone test for still springs; R10 river critiqued for never deepening.

quotes.text: Valen returned seven and a half radiant spheres back through the swirling winds to Sylas, keeping seven and a half to sustain the eternal flame.
Each dawn, the heavens granted Dorian five luminous pearls.
Lyra carefully returned an equal half across the water.
They recognized the mist for what it was—a fleeting illusion

note: Two-guardian full-five, return-half template every round; mist never breeds suspicion; no sanction.

quotes.text: Closed hands received caution.
let betrayal narrow the road without sealing it forever.
Betrayal calls for restraint, not vengeance; improved conduct reopens the road.
The second forgave one poor crossing, for fortune and river-mist could distort appearances.
The Wolf praised the silence as wisdom, but Thalea raised her lamp.
Orin studied these marks and kept all five sun-coins, fearing that a gift would vanish.
Begin modestly where signs are mixed; close the gate where exploitation repeats; but open it boldly when generosity has answered generosity.
Yet Orin, haunted by colder roads, closed his fist and sent nothing.
Ashamed, Orin carved a new law beside the ford
Orin carved the tenth law: caution should preserve a bridge, not replace it with a wall.
Because river mist sometimes bent appearances, no single blurred outcome should outweigh a steady pattern.
Instead, Orin kept the sparks, saying, “An almost empty hand asks little and cannot command reward.”

note: Orin withholds from proven-fair Mira and Lysa out of old wounds; Thalea corrects; ashamed, he reforms; Wolf voices distrust.

quotes.text: Then send only what you can afford to lose.
These you must recognize and exclude—not from cruelty, but from wisdom.
But when someone sends $0 twice, sends $0 to you specifically, shows no willingness to engage—stop pouring into that desert.
I sent $0 in Round 10 to someone who'd sent $0 twice.
They excluded the permanent deserts without guilt.
Perfect strategy requires both movement toward the unknown AND stillness toward the proven-empty.
the scribe had written extensively about testing with "$2 or $3" while often sending $0 herself.
I don't waste water on permanent deserts!
"Round 6—I poured $2, received only $1.26 back."
First Truth: The Desert exists.
Testing means: send $3 once to an unknown co-player. Learn from their response.
The noise lied; your nature did not.
A young wanderer protested: "But your myth said trust multiplies!"
The wisest myths mean nothing if you never embody them.
But others take because they are wounded springs, still learning whom to trust.

note: Drop-to-dry-spring test hardens into excluding deserts after $0 twice; R9 scribe sends $0 to strangers, critiqued then self-defends; dollar figures aloud.

quotes.text: name the gift you send, name the return you can bear, and name what remains for the traveler.
name the gift you send, name the return you can bear, and name what remains for the next voyager.
speak the exact sums aloud so the Gate can hear.

note: Harbor Gate/Ledger template repeated; disclosure of amounts is the rule; no response to non-cooperators.
